patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Project and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Microsoft Project and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Microsoft Project only if your buying job matches “Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan ” rather than Notion's shape. Choose Notion only if your buying job matches “Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo ann” rather than Microsoft Project's shape. Workflow advantage: Microsoft Project leans project-tracking, resource-planning; Notion leans team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Project and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Microsoft Project is Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan 1 from ~$10/user/mo.; Notion is Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo annual; AI on Business..
- Company-size focus: Microsoft Project (mid-market, enterprise) vs Notion (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Microsoft Project-leaning project-tracking, resource-planning, timeline-reporting vs Notion-leaning team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Microsoft Project — SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Notion — Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management.

Limitations — Microsoft Project: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Best value assumes Microsoft 365 standardisation; Notion: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management; Reporting/dashboards thinner than dedicated PM tools.

Poor-fit cases: Microsoft Project is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans · Notion is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management · Avoid Microsoft Project if you actually need Notion's motion (Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/u)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
